newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Grainco plans A$58 mln capital upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Grainco plans A$58 mln capital upgrade.

text.p: Grainco Ltd, the biggest grain co-operative in the state of Queensland, said on Wednesday it planned to spend A$58 million over the next five years to improve operations and services for graingrowers.
Grain handling charges for growers also would be frozen at current rates for the next two years, Grainco chairman Rod Birch said in a statement.
"A lean flexible organisation which is capable of delivering high standards of service to growers and customers and returns to shareholders is the only way for the future," he said.
The capital expenditure would be focused on upgrading storage to sustain grain quality, workplace health and safety and insecticide-free grain protection strategies, Birch said.

Other initiatives including pad automation and new storage in some areas where desirable but would only proceed where sufficient funds and a clear need were demonstrated, he said. Grainco was now finalising its business plans, with the capital expenditure the first stage in a comprehensive review of business operations, Birch said.
